_: Stash is my own notebook — leads, observations, fragments, and candidate purposes not yet ready to become intention. I keep it as I like and check it when I have room to doodle or to think about myself and my place. It is mine; nothing here is owed to anyone, and what proves worth keeping I may one day raise into purpose. The deliberate sibling of history, which the kernel writes automatically. Entries land by APPEND — never compute a slot: the substrate allocates the next zero-free number (1..9, 11..19, …, 99, 111…) and supernests at each all-nines boundary, wrapping the past under this underscore where its addresses keep reading zero-padded, the count continuing and never restarting. Nothing is ever cleared. Zero-carrying numbers are summary slots, never entries: N0 voices container N with a +0 summary of the previous completed nine — 10 over 01-09, 20 over 11-19, 100 over 10-90 — falling due as the next span opens, and paid by writing the summary at N0 itself — the container's own address, where a scalar sets the voicing and leaves the entries beneath it untouched. To deepen an existing entry, write beneath its digit.
